publications.title: Potential Benefits of Nobiletin, A Citrus Flavonoid, against Alzheimer's Disease and Parkinson's Disease.
publications.main_finding: Nobiletin improved cognitive deficits and pathological features of Alzheimer's disease, as well as motor and cognitive deficits in Parkinson's disease animal models.
publications.limitations: The study relies on animal models and does not provide clinical evidence in humans.

publications.title: Neuroprotection by dihydrotestosterone in LPS-induced neuroinflammation.

publications.title: Neuroprotection by saponins.

publications.title: Updates and advances in multiple sclerosis neurotherapeutics.
publications.main_finding: The multiple sclerosis neurotherapeutic landscape is evolving with new disease-modifying therapies and ongoing research into neuropathological targets for progressive MS.

publications.title: Coffee and multiple sclerosis (MS).
publications.main_finding: Coffee consumption, including compounds like caffeine, polyphenols, and diterpenes, may reduce inflammation and oxidative stress while enhancing neural function in MS patients.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not present original clinical trial data confirming the therapeutic efficacy of coffee in MS patients.

publications.title: In silico screening and preclinical validation identify bavisant as a therapeutic candidate for multiple sclerosis.
publications.main_finding: Bavisant, a histamine receptor H3 antagonist, promoted remyelination and neuroprotection in mouse models of demyelination and axonal injury.
publications.limitations: The study provides proof-of-concept in animal models but has not yet been validated in human clinical trials.

publications.title: From metabolism to mind: The expanding role of the GLP-1 receptor in neurotherapeutics.
publications.main_finding: GLP-1 receptor agonists are under investigation for neuroprotective effects in neurological disorders, though clinical trial outcomes have been variable due to study heterogeneity.
publications.limitations: The review does not provide definitive clinical evidence for the efficacy of GLP-1RAs in treating specific neurological diseases.

publications.title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Pathophysiological Mechanisms and Treatment Strategies (Part 2).
publications.main_finding: Recent advances in understanding ALS pathogenesis focus on glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity and oxidative stress, with therapeutic strategies targeting these mechanisms through antiglutamatergic and antioxidant drugs.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not provide specific clinical trial results or efficacy data for the mentioned therapeutic strategies.

publications.title: Biological and neurological activities of astaxanthin (Review).
publications.main_finding: Astaxanthin is a lipid-soluble carotenoid with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties that can cross the blood-brain barrier and may offer neuroprotective effects.
publications.limitations: The biological effects of astaxanthin on humans and its underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood.

publications.title: Current therapy in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS): A review on past and future therapeutic strategies.
publications.main_finding: Current ALS treatment options are limited to two FDA-approved drugs, riluzole and edavarone, neither of which provides a cure for the disease.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not provide new clinical data on the efficacy of the reviewed neuroprotective compounds.

publications.title: Riluzole for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
publications.main_finding: Riluzole is a benzothiazole derivative that blocks glutamatergic neurotransmission and prolongs tracheostomy-free survival in ALS patients by approximately 2-3 months.
publications.limitations: The clinical efficacy of riluzole in treating ALS is described as modest.

publications.title: Riluzole-induced recurrent pancreatitis.
publications.main_finding: Two patients with sporadic limb-onset ALS developed recurrent acute pancreatitis during treatment with riluzole.
publications.limitations: This report is based on only two cases and does not establish a definitive causal mechanism.

publications.title: Huntington's disease.
publications.main_finding: Molecular genetics has revealed the disease trigger for Huntington's disease as an inherited unstable CAG expansion in a novel 4p16.3 gene.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not provide results from clinical trials or specific drug efficacy data.

publications.title: Lithium and autophagy.
publications.main_finding: Lithium enhances degradation of aggregate-prone proteins and causes damaged mitochondria to degrade in various neuropsychiatric conditions.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not provide clinical trial outcomes confirming therapeutic benefit in patients.

publications.title: Synaptic versus extrasynaptic NMDA receptor signalling: implications for neurodegenerative disorders.
publications.main_finding: Stimulation of synaptic NMDARs leads to a neuroprotective shield, whereas stimulation of extrasynaptic NMDARs promotes cell death.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not report on the development or testing of specific neuroprotective therapies.

publications.title: Mitophagy in Huntington's disease.
publications.main_finding: Inefficient removal of damaged mitochondria is thought to contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases such as Huntington's disease.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not present experimental data on the pharmacological regulation of mitophagy.

publications.title: Update on rivastigmine.
publications.main_finding: Rivastigmine is an effective therapeutic agent for treating cognitive and behavioral symptoms in Alzheimer disease and diffuse Lewy body disease.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not provide original clinical data but summarizes findings from previously conducted trials.

publications.title: [New therapeutic approaches].
publications.main_finding: Novel treatment approaches for dementia are aimed at preventing, slowing, or ameliorating the production, aggregation, and deposition of pathological proteins.
publications.limitations: This review does not report specific clinical outcomes or efficacy results for the mentioned therapeutic strategies.

publications.title: Lysophospholipids: A Potential Drug Candidates for Neurodegenerative Disorders.
publications.main_finding: Porcine liver decomposition product-derived lysophospholipids may potentially inhibit alpha-synuclein aggregation in neurodegenerative disorders.
publications.limitations: The precise mechanisms by which lipids prevent pathological alpha-synuclein aggregation require further clarification.

publications.title: Identification of small molecule dimethyoxyphenyl piperazine inhibitors of alpha-synuclein fibril growth.
publications.main_finding: Two dimethoxyphenyl piperazine analogs were identified that potently inhibit the growth of in-vitro assembled alpha-synuclein fibrils.
publications.limitations: The study was conducted in vitro and does not demonstrate efficacy in human subjects.

publications.title: Cholinergic white matter pathways integrity in prodromal and early manifest Lewy body disease.
publications.main_finding: Higher microstructural integrity of nucleus basalis of Meynert white matter pathways is associated with better cognitive performance and reduced risk of phenoconversion in isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder.
publications.limitations: No significant differences in microstructural integrity were observed between patient cohorts and controls at baseline.

publications.title: Microglia in neurodegeneration.
publications.main_finding: Microglia perform sentinel, housekeeping, and defense functions, and an imbalance between these functions contributes to the initiation or exacerbation of neurodegeneration.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not provide specific clinical data or experimental results from a primary study.

publications.title: Mitochondria in neurodegeneration.
publications.main_finding: Mitochondrial pathology is strongly implicated in chronic neurodegenerative diseases, involving complex relationships across the mitochondrial life cycle.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not present new experimental findings or clinical trial outcomes.

publications.title: Progressive supranuclear palsy.
publications.main_finding: Progressive supranuclear palsy is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by 4 repeat tau deposition, with current therapeutic options being symptomatic and insufficient.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not report on the efficacy of any specific new treatment.

publications.title: Molecular mechanisms and consequences of TDP-43 phosphorylation in neurodegeneration.
publications.main_finding: The role of TDP-43 phosphorylation in neurodegeneration is site and context dependent, with conflicting evidence suggesting it may either drive disease or serve a neuroprotective role.

publications.title: Gamma Entrainment Binds Higher-Order Brain Regions and Offers Neuroprotection.
publications.main_finding: Chronic daily gamma entrainment using sensory stimuli preserved neuronal and synaptic density and modified cognitive performance in Tau P301S and CK-p25 mouse models.
publications.limitations: The findings are based on mouse models and have not been demonstrated in human subjects.

publications.title: Multiple system atrophy: advances in pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment.
publications.main_finding: Progress in understanding α-synuclein seeding and strains has informed revised diagnostic criteria for multiple system atrophy.
publications.limitations: No clinical trial has yet provided unequivocal evidence of neuroprotection for this disease.

publications.title: Progressive supranuclear palsy.
publications.main_finding: New clinical diagnostic criteria for progressive supranuclear palsy account for phenotypic variability to improve early diagnosis.

publications.title: Interventions in progressive supranuclear palsy.
publications.main_finding: Recent studies of davunetide and tideglusib failed to improve the clinical outcome of patients with progressive supranuclear palsy.
publications.limitations: No effective symptomatic or neuroprotective treatment is currently available for progressive supranuclear palsy.

publications.title: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and Statin Use.
publications.main_finding: Statins may have inverse associations with progressive supranuclear palsy risk and motor impairment.

publications.title: [Neuroprotective treatment of tauopathies].

publications.title: Multiple system atrophy: advances in pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment.
publications.main_finding: Progress in understanding α-synuclein pathophysiology and revised diagnostic criteria have improved the potential for early diagnosis and development of disease-modifying therapies for multiple system atrophy.

publications.title: REM sleep behaviour disorder.
publications.main_finding: REM sleep behaviour disorder is a parasomnia characterized by loss of muscle atonia during REM sleep and is recognized as a manifestation of an α-synucleinopathy.
publications.limitations: The abstract does not provide results from specific clinical trials evaluating neuroprotective therapies in patients with idiopathic RBD.

publications.title: Risk and predictors of dementia and parkinsonism in idiopathic REM sleep behaviour disorder: a multicentre study.

publications.title: Multiple system atrophy.

publications.title: REM sleep behavior disorder: update on diagnosis and management.

publications.title: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) mediated mRNA delivery in neurodegenerative diseases.

publications.title: Aging, Neurodegenerative Disorders, and Cerebellum.
publications.main_finding: The cerebellum is involved in motor control and cognition, and its function is disrupted during aging and various neurodegenerative disorders.

publications.title: Progress and challenges in sporadic late-onset cerebellar ataxias.

publications.title: Mitochondrial ferritin in neurodegenerative diseases.
